title: Counterexample Search and Falsification
description: Popper's demarcation: a claim earns scientific status by surviving attempts to refute it. The cross-examiner's first move is always the hunt for the counterexample — one black swan sinks 'all swans are white'.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
lo=1; hi=50
# Claim: f(x) = x^2 - 3x + 2 > 0 for all x in [lo,hi]. Cross-examine by fuzzing.
def f(x): return x*x - 3*x + 2
violations=[x for x in range(lo,hi+1) if not f(x) > 0]
print(f"claim: f(x)>0 on [1,50]")
print(f"counterexamples_found={len(violations)} first={violations[:5]}")
print(f"verdict={'REFUTED' if violations else 'SURVIVED fuzzing'}")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
claim: f(x)>0 on [1,50]
counterexamples_found=2 first=[1, 2]
verdict=REFUTED
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Claims are parsed into quantified statements; the searcher generates boundary and random cases hunting violations. A single verified counterexample refutes the universal claim and is filed with its witness.
implementation_status: Public method, established (Popper 1959). Prototype validated in this build (executed 2026-10-21).

acceptance_tests.test: False universal claim refuted with witness
True claim survives the fuzz battery
